newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on dollar profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on dollar profit-taking.

text.p: The won closed higher against the U.S. currency on Wednesday on dollar profit-taking by Korean companies, dealers said.
"The dollar needs a rest following recent steep rises," said a foreign bank dealer. "Domestic companies, building up the greenback from 850 won to 870 won, tried to take profits."

Dealers said an expected inflow of foreign funds for stock investment also chilled dollar buying interest. South Korea will raise the foreign stock holding limit to 23 percent from May 2 against 20 percent at present.
The won ended at 893.90 against Tuesday's close of 895.00.
After opening at 895.00, the won hit a day high of 893.50 and a low of 895.50.
"The won/dollar rate is expected to be confined to a tight range tomorrow," said a domestic bank dealer, forecasting the dollar would move in an 893.00-895.50 range.
The foreign bank dealer said the dollar consolidation would continue for two months, but he ruled out a sharp fall of the dollar.
Thursday's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 894.50 against 895.40 today.
